evidence.quote: Today the FOMC decided that the cumulative effects of those developments over the last several months warrant a patient, wait-and-see approach regarding future policy changes.
Inflation readings have been muted, and the recent drop in oil prices is likely to push headline inflation lower still in coming months.
In addition, the case for raising rates has weakened somewhat.
The implication is that the normalization of the size of the portfolio will be completed sooner, and with a larger balance sheet, than in previous estimates.
But the crosscurrents I mentioned suggest the risk of a less favorable outlook.
The jobs picture continues to be strong, with the unemployment rate near historic lows and with stronger wage gains.

parsed.rationale: Rates held, but the Chair signals a clear pause in hikes ('patient'), says the case for raising rates has weakened, highlights muted inflation and downside crosscurrents, and signals an earlier end to runoff with a larger balance sheet. Strong labor market description tempers but does not offset the dovish shift.
